subject: Scheduling: Technical architecture handshake for Redwood integration with QuantumBridge
messages:
From: Kyle Hart <kyle.hart@quantumbridge.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Lina Alvarez <lina.alvarez@quantumbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 15:07:00 -0800
Subject: Post-discovery: next step for architecture session

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the discovery call earlier today — Lina and I walked away confident Redwood can address our inference latency and cost concerns. Our PM asked for a focused technical session with people who will own the integration (network, infra, and SRE).

Can we align on a ~60-minute architecture handshake next week? Top goals for us:
- Validate VPC connectivity options (shared VPC vs peering)
- Confirm auth/secret handling (KMS/HSM)
- Understand model routing and fallback behavior under load

Attendees on our side: Lina (platform lead), myself (CTO), plus our infra engineer (TBD). Ideal times are Tue/Wed 10am–1pm PT or Thurs afternoon.

I attached our discovery notes.

Best,
Kyle

Attachment: QBridge_discovery_notes.pdf
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Kyle Hart <kyle.hart@quantumbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 16:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: next step for architecture session

Kyle — great to hear. Thanks for the notes and the clear goals. I copied Marissa (account lead) and Ben (solutions engineer) so we can line up the right folks and prep materials.

Quick proposal: 60 minutes with the following agenda:
1) Quick introductions + scope (5m)
2) VPC/networking options & recommended configs (15m)
3) Auth, keys, and audit trail (10m)
4) Model routing/fallover + expected SLOs under load (20m)
5) Action items & next steps (10m)

Times that work for our team:
- Wed 12/2 10:30–11:30 AM PT
- Wed 12/2 12:00–1:00 PM PT
- Thu 12/3 2:00–3:00 PM PT

If none of those fit, please share a slot and we’ll be flexible. Also, can you confirm the infra engineer’s email so we can send a calendar invite with a pre-read?

I attached a short technical checklist we’ll use to prepare.

—Olga

Attachment: redwood-techtouch-checklist.docx
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, Kyle Hart <kyle.hart@quantumbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: next step for architecture session

Adding some prep notes from the SE side — hi Kyle, Ben from Redwood here. A few items I want to confirm before the session so we can make the call productive:
- Desired RTO/RPO and target p99 latency for production traffic (if you have numbers please share)
- Expected token sizes / avg and max sequence lengths (rough estimates are fine)
- Are you planning to use our hosted API, Dedicated, or Private deployment? If Private, is this VPC peering or on-prem?
- Any firewall egress rules or proxy that could affect TLS handshakes?

I'll prepare: sample network diagrams for each deployment mode, a short runbook for KMS integration, and an example routing policy for model fallback. If you can drop the infra engineer's email and a rough attendee list, we’ll attach the invite and the pre-read.

Thanks — Ben
From: Kyle Hart <kyle.hart@quantumbridge.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Lina Alvarez <lina.alvarez@quantumbridge.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 17:50:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: next step for architecture session

Thanks, Ben and Olga. Wed 12/2 12:00–1:00 PM PT works for our group — Lina and I will be there, and we’ll bring our infra engineer, Samir Patel (samir.patel@quantumbridge.com).

Quick answers:
- Target p99: <= 400ms for inference under nominal load; burst tolerance to 800ms
- Avg token length: ~120 tokens; peaks up to ~600 tokens in some calls
- Deployment preference: Hosted API to start, with Dedicated for high-throughput pipelines later
- We have an outbound proxy that terminates TLS inside our VPC; we’ll confirm exact egress IPs before the call

Please send the calendar invite and any pre-reads. Also we need to cover any SOC2 evidence flow — Lina will bring that up during the call.

—Kyle
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Kyle Hart <kyle.hart@quantumbridge.com>, samir.patel@quantumbridge.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 11:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Confirmed: Wed 12/2 12:00–1:00 PM PT — Technical architecture handshake (calendar invite + pre-read)

Kyle / Samir / Lina — confirmed for Wed 12/2 12:00–1:00 PM PT (I booked the 12:00–1:00 slot and shared the calendar invite; if you don't see it, please check spam or the shared calendar).

Pre-read attached and quick checklist:
- Please review sections: Networking (pages 2–3), Auth & KMS (page 5), Model routing & fallback (page 7).
- For the call: have sample p99 numbers and one example payload for token size testing ready.
- Security: we will cover SOC2 evidence flow and what logs/artifacts we can provide for procurement.

Attachments: redwood-techtouch-checklist.docx
Action items before session:
- QuantumBridge: confirm egress IPs (Samir)
- Redwood: send network diagrams + expected TLS endpoints (Ben)
- Marissa: follow up on procurement timeline and any contractual questions (marissa_cole@redwood.ai)

If anything changes I’ll update the invite. Looking forward to the call — we’ll keep it tightly scoped and leave time for SOC2/procurement questions at the end.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182
